main_text.p: verba Pf. 144.8.&11.de juramento intelligunt, Quorum os loquitur vanitatem, &dextra eorum est dextra iniquitatis, vel potius mendacii sive falsitatis; id enim proprie significant Hebraea [?]ימין שקר. Quin & ipse Deus ubi ad modum humanum [?]ἀνθρωποπαθῶς inducitur, eo loquendi genere utitur. Ego levo ad coelum manum meam, & juro in dextra mea, Deut. 32.40, ad quem ritum & alibi in libris Propheticis utriusque Testamenti non raro allusum. Quem proinde ritum iterum jure miremini, in Christianis Ecclesiis non tolerari modo, sed & approbari ab ipsissimis illis viris, qui tamen alios veteris Testamenti ritus (cum sint ejusdem rationis omnes, aut liciti pariter, aut pariter illiciti,) à Christianis ita, ut ne tolerent quidem, sed è sacris penitus exterminandos clamitent. Quod attinet ad ritus Christianorum, ut reliquas Ecclesiae ceremonias varias, varietate pro locorum & temporum varietate observatas missas faciam: Vna fere est quae a prisco seculo ad nos usque devata, etiamnum in usu est, sc. ut tactis [?]sacrosanctis Dei Evangeliis in verba concepta juretur. Et hoc omne genus

page.notes: The left edge of the column is clipped, so the first letters of several lines are partly cut off (for example "ligunt", "nim", "ariter", "ifurpari", "rifcæ", "ft quæ", "ivata"). I have read them from the context and the full words are as printed. The Hebrew "ימין שקר" and the Greek "ἀνθρωποπαθῶς" are read from a small scan and are uncertain; the vowel marks and accents are not clear. The word "sacrosanctis" is inferred from the clipped fragment "icrofanctis". The word "ut" before "ne tolerent" is blurred and may be read differently. The line "Vna fere est quae" is partly cut off at its beginning. The printed "Pf." and "devata" are copied as printed, with "devata" as the likely reading of a blurred word.
